feature: Copying an icon puts its SVG on the clipboard
summary: Copying a drawing now puts the same SVG Export writes for a web page on the clipboard, beside the picture. Pasting into a Chrome-based app hands it the shapes; pasting into a chat or TextEdit still gives the picture.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: On a blank canvas choose New Frame, pick 24 under Icons, click Add Frame.
Press E for the ellipse tool and drag a circle inside the frame.
Click the frame inside, outside the circle, so the frame is picked, then press Command C.
Paste into a Chrome page that reads the clipboard: it is offered image/svg+xml, a 24 by 24 file with whole-unit numbers.
Press Escape, then Shift Command C, and paste into TextEdit (rich): the picture lands, as before.
Open a screenshot and press Shift Command C: the clipboard holds the picture only, with no SVG.

evaluate: Does Command C on a picked icon frame feel like the natural way to copy an icon?
Is it right that Shift Command C on a whole canvas copies a 1600 by 1100 SVG with the icon placed where it sits, rather than just the icon?
Would you expect Figma to take the shapes on paste from this clipboard? It could not be tried here without pasting into a real web service.
rough: No mock covers the clipboard, so there is no side by side; the shot is the canvas at the moment of copying.

A code editor, a plain text box and Safari never see the SVG file type, so pasting there gives nothing. Putting the code on as text would take the slot the measurement list uses: decision card an-icon-svg-pastes-into-a-code-editor-how-should-a-copied-icon-s-svg-c, task an-icon-svg-pastes-into-a-code-editor.
Command C on a single picked shape (the circle alone) carries no SVG: only a frame, or the whole drawing, is something Export writes. The circle copies as a layer, as before.

A picked frame copies with its own white surface in the SVG, exactly as Export writes that frame; whether an icon should keep that white is the open card on task copying-an-icon-carries-the-white-canvas-the-exp.

Figma, VS Code and the real TextEdit app were not driven by hand: Figma is a web service, and driving the other two would have taken the keyboard from whoever is at the Mac. Chrome 153, WebKit and TextEdit's own text view were measured instead (docs/design/references/svg-copy-check).
